holidays.name: National Watermelon Day
holidays.description: Grab a fork, a spoon, or just your face. Today is for celebrating the juicy, drippy, seed-spitting king of summer fruits. Slice it, cube it, grill it, blend it into a slushie, or sprinkle it with salt and chili. Anything goes, as long as it's watermelon.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial food observance with no single known founder. It has become a fixture of the American summer food calendar, timed for the peak of watermelon season.
holidays.funFact: Watermelon is about 92 percent water. It's also related to cucumbers, pumpkins, and squash. Some early Egyptian tomb paintings appear to show watermelons, so people have been enjoying them for thousands of years.

holidays.name: National Grab Some Nuts Day
holidays.description: This is a snack holiday with a cheeky name. You're invited to grab a handful of your favorite nuts, whether that's almonds, pistachios, cashews, walnuts, or peanuts. Crunch away and call it a health move.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial observance of unclear origin. It encourages people to celebrate and snack on all kinds of nuts.
holidays.funFact: Peanuts aren't true nuts. They're legumes that grow underground, which makes them cousins of peas and lentils. Cashews, meanwhile, grow dangling from the bottom of a fruit called the cashew apple.
